analyst_view.overall: Lugano top the Conference League table with 9 points from 3 games (11 scored, 4 conceded), while Jablonec are 23rd on 2 points with no win in Europe after 2-3 at Freiburg, 0-0 with Brighton and 1-1 at Riga. Lugano's club and Swiss media reported on Wednesday that Albian Ajeti's ban is domestic only, so he can play here, while the numbers still take him out as suspended (about -16% on Lugano's goals); match-day checks (UEFA's match page and others) found nothing that changes that, and line-ups were not out at writing. Both sides play league games on Sunday and a team-news preview expects some rotation; Lugano also list midfielder Vuklisevic as out and Hannes Delcroix is injured (counted). Jablonec are without keeper Jan Hanus and captain Tekijaski, with Klemen Mihelak in goal and Cedidla moved into central defence; Hanus and Milla are already in the numbers. Referee David Smajc (6.0 cards a game in a small sample) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals but take about 16% off Lugano's scoring for Ajeti as suspended, while Swiss reports say his ban covers only domestic games and he is free for Thursday. I add most of that back, to about 3.3, but not all of it, as Croci-Torti has said he will rotate with a league game on Sunday and Jablonec have been hard to score against at home in Europe.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners, 5.4 for Jablonec, who need a first European win and attack with crosses at home, with both sides' recent corner counts already in. Ajeti's return changes Lugano's finishing rather than how much of the ball they have, and a few rotated players should not change their wide play, so I stay at 9.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards, already adding about 6% for referee David Smajc (6.0 a game in two on record) and more for both sides' recent bookings. Ajeti's red card was in the Swiss league and these clubs have never met, so nothing points to an unusually heated game and I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots, a fairly open game, already lifted a little for Jablonec's recent volume. Ajeti's return helps Lugano's finishing more than their number of shots, and the rotation expected before Sunday pulls slightly the other way, so I stay at 30.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. Jablonec's stand-in keeper Mihelak (Hanus is counted) and Ajeti's availability matter more for how many go in than for how many are on target, so I stay at 9.2.
